scope: Actual compiled UI and isolated SQLite API/worker; only discovery and virtual transport are redirected to owned loopback processes. Generated accounts, not public demo credentials.
checks: Player signs in to the assigned Roma team; own preparation excludes peer profiles and the phone/tablet home fits.
Home availability changes receive actual service acknowledgement and update the own-player view.
Player can switch upcoming/past matches and training, download only a chosen calendar event, and past match replies are read-only.
Player profile exposes only its own membership/preferences, and an actual FA-ID save persists without a staff role.
Player statistics have one bound player and no teammate selector; detail and unknown-data coverage remain own-only.
Player can open team overview and shared game updates without match-controller controls.
Player feedback is own-only and closed historic games do not display editors.
Player can read permitted team/opposition summaries and its own reports without staff controls.
Player photos show only permitted albums, and no staff moderation controls are exposed; ballot window metadata remains explicit.
Player can reach scoped spectator invitations and account controls; no invitation capability is captured.
Player sign out ends the actual session and closes private home/stat views.
A prospective Player can request the exact club/team; staff receive a pending request without a new login, membership or child-account approval.
findings: Current seed correctly has no eligible same-day completed game: open feedback editing needs a separately labelled reducer-completed fixture; closed history/privacy are exercised here.
Current completed seed games have closed ballots; no voting window is invented for this review.
